paths.description: Public search homepage and initial consent state; represents the primary landing and search-entry template.
Primary search journey from query entry to results; execution reached Google anti-automation CAPTCHA, so end-to-end result quality could not be judged.
Advanced Search form; represents the form-heavy search refinement template.

findings.summary: The consent dialog interrupts and obscures the primary search task on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and crawler screenshots show a large modal covering the central search surface before interaction, although Reject all and Accept all are equally prominent.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the least intrusive legally compliant consent surface, preserve immediate access to essential search, and retain equal, declarative dismiss choices.

findings.summary: Primary state and document changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The DOM/platform probe found no view-transition declaration and the search interaction video shows a direct state update rather than a guided transition.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained same-document and cross-document View Transitions for search suggestions and navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The homepage omits a viewport meta tag, so a 360px device receives a 980px layout scaled down to 0.367.
findings.evidence: layout-mobile.json reports hasViewportMeta false, layout/client width 980 at a requested 360x800 viewport; the mobile screenshot shows the entire desktop page and consent text shrunk to tiny scale.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and let the layout reflow intrinsically at the device width without disabling zoom.

findings.summary: Observed layouts do not use component-level container responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The page probe found no CSS container rules and the advanced-search form uses a fixed 484px content/form width in its DOM evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable search/form groups so they adapt to available component space rather than fixed widths.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the primary search field, and several targets are below 44px.
findings.evidence: The focused textarea computed outline is none and box-shadow none; the probe lists multiple 16-40px-high links, buttons and search affordances.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible indicator and increase target hit areas to at least 44x44 CSS px where practical.

findings.summary: The minimalist homepage still transfers 700KB of JavaScript and retains avoidable render-path work.
findings.evidence: HAR summary reports 800,512 transferred bytes, including 700,025 script bytes; Lighthouse flags the dependency tree/render-blocking insight.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical dependency chains and defer or conditionally load nonessential homepage modules.

findings.summary: The page ships measurable unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 56KiB unused JavaScript and 11KiB unused CSS on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Split feature bundles and styles by actual homepage use, and conditionally load secondary features after intent.

findings.summary: Some inline links do not maintain sufficient distinguishability from surrounding text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.96 and failed link-in-text-block; this is the only automated accessibility failure recorded.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure links in prose are distinguishable without relying on color alone and meet text/background contrast requirements.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a main landmark and a visible focus treatment on the primary field.
findings.evidence: The accessibility probe found zero main landmarks and computed no outline or shadow after focusing the search textarea.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main and provide a persistent, high-contrast :focus-visible style that follows reading order.

findings.summary: Zoom/reflow and target sizing are undermined by the missing viewport declaration and undersized controls.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout is rendered at 980 CSS px and scaled to 0.367; the target probe identifies many controls below 44px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a scalable viewport declaration, verify reflow at 320-400px, and enlarge interactive hit areas.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic width and height attributes.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports 7 of 7 img elements without width/height; Lighthouse also flags unsized-images, although measured CLS was 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare intrinsic width and height (or an equivalent aspect-ratio reservation) for every image.

findings.summary: The homepage has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The page probe returns description null and Lighthouse SEO fails meta-description, reducing its SEO score to 0.92.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, locale-appropriate meta description describing Google Search.

findings.summary: Mobile crawlability quality is reduced by the missing viewport meta tag.
findings.evidence: The homepage has real href links and robots permits the localized homepage, but both DOM and layout probes confirm no viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standard responsive viewport meta declaration while preserving crawlable anchors and robots access.

findings.summary: Localized homepage indexing signals omit canonical and hreflang declarations.
findings.evidence: The page probe found no canonical URL, while the rendered language is en-GB on a localized google.com.hk host; robots and HTTP status were otherwise healthy.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare a canonical policy and hreflang alternates for localized homepage variants where those variants are intended for indexing.

findings.summary: The public organization/search homepage exposes no structured or social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The page probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and basic Open Graph metadata that matches visible content.

findings.summary: The main document lacks several baseline defensive response headers.
findings.evidence: headers.json confirms HTTPS and SAMEORIGIN framing but reports missing CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforced CSP, HSTS, nosniff and a deliberate Referrer-Policy; retain clickjacking and Permissions-Policy controls.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The response has X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN and Permissions-Policy unload=(), but no HSTS, CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy or nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Complete the defensive policy set with HSTS, CSP including frame-ancestors and Trusted Types where viable, nosniff, and explicit referrer/permission controls.

findings.summary: The localized UI relies heavily on physical directional CSS rather than logical properties.
findings.evidence: The platform probe counted 238 physical left/right declarations and the page probe found no observed logical inline/block styling.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace directional layout declarations with logical properties so translated RTL and alternate writing-mode layouts remain robust.

findings.summary: Script weight and unused code are disproportionate to the simple search landing surface.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 700,025 script bytes for a minimal form page and Lighthouse estimates 56KiB unused JS plus 11KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a homepage resource budget, eliminate unused modules, and defer work until user intent requires it.

findings.summary: Third-party and supporting-origin resources add about 90KB to the initial page.
findings.evidence: HAR summary reports 8 third-party requests and 90,624 third-party bytes, chiefly gstatic, on an otherwise compact visual surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit supporting-origin modules and fonts, cache aggressively, and load nonessential third-party resources only after intent.

taskList.title: Add a scalable responsive viewport and verify genuine 320-400px reflow.
Restore keyboard focus visibility, a main landmark, and adequate hit areas.
Deploy CSP, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and complete browser defense headers.
Reduce and conditionally load homepage JavaScript, CSS, and supporting-origin modules.
Make the consent experience less obstructive while preserving equal Reject/Accept choices.
Add a locale-appropriate meta description, canonical/hreflang policy, JSON-LD, and social metadata.
Declare intrinsic dimensions for all images.
Replace physical left/right CSS with logical properties.
Introduce container responsiveness for reusable search and form groups.
Add restrained View Transitions with reduced-motion handling.
